item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Abiy’s 2024 record on 8B.5 is mixed but tilts negative. There is real evidence of follow-through and coordination in the macroeconomic reform track and some cross-agency service delivery, but the security and internal-control record is dominated by emergency centralization, parallel coercive structures, repression of watchdogs, and weak accountability. Direct public evidence on routine party discipline and day-to-day inter-ministry coordination is limited, so the judgment leans on these proxies.

**Accepted Claims**
- **The Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia: First Review Under the Extended Credit Facility Arrangement** — IMF, 2024-11-04. Claim: Ethiopia met all quantitative performance criteria and 4 of 5 structural benchmarks, while the exchange-rate transition kept progressing and the official/parallel market gap narrowed. This is strong evidence of technical follow-through in the economic file and coordination with reform institutions. URL: https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2024/11/04/the-federal-democratic-republic-of-ethiopia-first-review-under-the-extended-credit-facility-557019. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **World Bank Backs Ethiopia’s Reforms to Promote Sustainable and Inclusive Growth, Enhance Resilience, and Take Climate Action** — World Bank, 2024-07-30. Claim: the reform package tied together fiscal transparency, financial-sector competition, SOE performance, public spending effectiveness, and social safety nets. This is good evidence of cross-ministry implementation discipline in the economic and social-policy areas. URL: https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/07/30/world-bank-backs-ethiopia-s-reforms-to-promote-sustainable-and-inclusive-afe-growth. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **Ethiopia launches inclusive ID system for refugees, boosts access to national services** — UNHCR Africa, 2024-03-07. Claim: the Refugees and Returnees Service, the National ID Program, and UNHCR rolled out digital IDs for refugees to improve access to services and prevent duplicate registration. This is concrete evidence of coordination across implementing agencies and a relatively disciplined administrative rollout. URL: https://www.unhcr.org/africa/news/press-releases/ethiopia-launches-inclusive-id-system-refugees-boosts-access-national-services. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **Ethiopian Justice Minister Briefs Diplomats about Transitional Justice Policy Implementation** — ENA, 2024-12-14. Claim: the ministry said it had moved the transitional-justice policy into an implementation phase with a roadmap, timelines, responsibilities, and legal frameworks for independent institutions. This is positive, but still mostly roadmap-level evidence rather than proof of durable implementation. URL: https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/eng_5626876. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **ICRC Impact in Ethiopia: January - June 2024 Bulletin** — International Committee of the Red Cross, 2024-09-13. Claim: the ICRC said it trained ENDF officers, judges, militia members, and local authorities on IHL and IHRL, with the stated aim of protecting civilians and medical personnel. This is limited positive evidence that parts of the coercive apparatus were being brought under common rules and procedures. URL: https://www.icrc.org/en/article/ethiopia-bulletin-january-june-2024. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **In Ethiopia, a secret committee orders killings and arrests to crush rebels** — Reuters via Ethiopian Human Rights Commission, 2024-02-27. Claim: the EHRC confirmed the existence of Koree Nageenyaa and said it overreached by interfering in the justice system with widespread rights violations. This is strong negative evidence of parallel coercive governance outside normal institutional discipline. URL: https://ehrc.org/in-ethiopia-a-secret-committee-orders-killings-and-arrests-to-crush-rebels-reuters/. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **Ethiopia: Halt Crackdown Against Human Rights Groups** — Human Rights Watch, 2024-06-18. Claim: security and intelligence personnel followed, intimidated, and threatened human-rights workers since February 2024, preventing independent scrutiny and chilling reporting. This points to control by intimidation rather than disciplined, accountable coordination. URL: https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/06/18/ethiopia-halt-crackdown-against-human-rights-groups. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **Details of State of Emergency Declared by Gov't of Ethiopia** — ENA, 2024-11-03. Claim: the proclamation centralized enforcement under a State of Emergency Operation Command, authorized replacement of local administrators, and suspended ordinary judicial authority over enforcement. This shows strong central coercive control, but it also cuts against normal institutional autonomy and transparent follow-through. URL: https://www.ena.et/web/eng/w/en_30124. QIDs: 8B.5.

- **Ethiopia rejects allegations its forces massacred civilians as the West urges an investigation** — Associated Press, 2024-02-15. Claim: Ethiopian officials denied Merawi massacre allegations while rights bodies said at least 45 civilians were killed and urged investigation. This is negative evidence for accountability and follow-through in the face of serious abuse allegations. URL: https://ktvz.com/news/ap-national-news/2024/02/15/ethiopia-rejects-allegations-its-forces-massacred-civilians-as-the-west-urges-an-investigation/. QIDs: 8B.5.

**Search gap**
I did not find direct public evidence showing routine internal party discipline or day-to-day coordination across all ministries, regions, and security organs. The available record is mostly indirect: formal reform follow-through in economics and transitional justice on the positive side, and emergency-rule centralization, covert security governance, and repression on the negative side.
